newsitem.title: NIGERIA: World Bank man sees Nigeria debt relief far off.
newsitem.headline: World Bank man sees Nigeria debt relief far off.

text.p: A World Bank executive on Tuesday assessed Nigeria's 1997 budget and concluded that the policies in place were not enough to attract badly-need debt relief.
"People often ask how long before Nigeria obtains the debt relief it needs," said Thomas Hutcheson, senior economist of the World Bank mission in Nigeria at a post-budget seminar in Lagos.
"They should rather ask how soon Nigeria will carry out reforms needed to reduce poverty, stimulate equitable growth and promote both foreign and domestic investments," he added.
Among the policies he criticised were the dual currency exchange rate and delay in privatising loss-making state enterprises.

Before the budget was announced last month, Nigerian officials had said privatisation was going to be embarked upon in 1997 and that the official rate of exchange which values the naira at four times its market rate would be scrapped.
Hutcheson also criticised the accounting procedures used to arrive at Nigeria's budget figures and said transparency was still lacking in reporting government incomes and expenditures.

"For many years there have been gaps in the budget presentation that 1997 did not correct," he said, adding "to point out these gaps is not to deny the real progress that has been made in creating a comprehensive budget."
Nigeria's foreign debt stock stood at $28 billion at the end of last year and its military government has voted $2 billion for debt repayment this year, the same as last year.
The government says it needs debt relief to be able to cope with its foreign debt burden but to get that it needs the World Bank to endorse its medium term economic programme.
Hutcheson said Nigeria needed to carry out the necessary policy reforms that would yield faster economic growth and reduce poverty of its citizens.

"These are the very policies that will inspire the confidence of Nigeria's creditors needed for debt relief," he said, adding "Whenever the government chooses to adopt these policies, the World Bank stands ready to assist Nigeria in the process."
